text:
Alex (Product): Quick sync — pricing/packaging ask from a handful of enterprise POCs. They want a 'priority burst' add-on for guaranteed cold-start GPU pools + priority routing. Need tradeoffs, launch criteria, and a recommended limits model by EOW. How risky is this to our margins and SLOs?
Priya (Sales): +1. 3 customers mentioned they'd sign a 12m commit if we can guarantee burst windows and soft guarantees on latency. They want a purchasable add-on instead of custom contracts.
Jordan (Finance): We need concrete uplift math. Suggest: add-on = +30% list price or fixed $/reserved-slot. Also require minimum commit to enable guaranteed capacity. Need projected margin impact if we reserve capacity.
Mei (Eng): Technical notes: priority routing + reserved cold pools means dedicated reserved nodes or prewarmed instances. Options: (a) carve dedicated pool per customer (expensive), (b) shared priority pool with strict admission control, (c) warm standby instances. Each has different TTM and cost. Rough estimate: 6–8 wks for infra + capacity testing for (b).
Sam (Legal): We can't promise "guaranteed" latency without detailed failure modes. Recommend SLA language: "best-effort priority routing; when capacity constraints occur we provide credits and fallbacks to compatible model variants". Also require CLRs (change log rights) and a cap on uptime credits.
Elena (Customer Success): Onboarding overhead will increase. We need a support SKU or playbook: white-glove setup, runbook for capacity thresholds, and a customer runbook for graceful fallback. Ask: who owns runbook? Eng + CS pairing.
Alex (Product): Draft launch criteria proposal — please react with :thumbsup: to confirm or add edits. 1) Business: committed ARR >= $X/mo to qualify OR explicit contract add-on purchase. 2) Finance: modeled +10% net margin uplift (min) after reserved cost. 3) Engineering: validated load tests for 99th percentile latency under burst scenarios + autoscale safety nets. 4) Legal: SLA and credit language approved. 5) CS: onboarding checklist + 2 pilot customers trained.
Priya (Sales): Suggest soft-cap model: customers get N burst tokens/month. Tokens consumed per burst-minute. Overage billed at premium. Cooldown window to avoid abuse. Keeps costs predictable.
Jordan (Finance): Token model okay, but need to set token price tied to marginal GPU cost. Also add minimum commit to offset zero-usage risk.
Mei (Eng): Implementation sketch:
```
priority_pool: 
  size: dynamic or reserved
  admission: token_bucket per-customer
  fallback: compatible-model-variant (lower perf)
```
Token bucket helps enforcement. We also need monitoring hooks and autoscale runbooks.
Sam (Legal): Also include termination & migration clauses for priority pools in case of sustained overload. No open-ended resource promises.
Alex (Product): Proposed limits we can surface in the UI: - monthly burst tokens - max concurrent bursts - cooldown minutes - auto-fallback toggle. Also pricing tiers: Performance Pack (tiered tokens) vs Enterprise Priority (dedicated pools + SLA).
Elena (Customer Success): For pilots, prefer Performance Pack first (shared priority pool) to validate demand before committing to dedicated pools.
Priya (Sales): I'll draft a go-to-market 1-pager and price anchors. Need eng + finance numbers to finalize.
Jordan (Finance): I'll run a Monte Carlo model on usage-to-cost next day, will share expected margin bands.
Mei (Eng): Risk checklist: 1) noisy neighbors in shared pool 2) preemption complexity 3) cache warmness & cold-start variance 4) billing accuracy for token usage. Need feature flags to gate rollout.
Alex (Product): Action items by owners + deadlines: 
- Priya: draft pricing anchors (tomorrow EOD)
- Jordan: cost/margin model (48h)
- Mei: implementation rough design + risk mitigation plan (EOW)
- Sam: SLA/contract template notes (EOW)
- Elena: pilot onboarding checklist (EOW)
I'll consolidate into a launch-readiness checklist and share for final signoff.
ops-bot: Deployment note: scheduled capacity experiment cluster #priority-burst-test at 2050007000.
Priya (Sales): One more ask — include optional "fast-path" network peering for customers behind strict networking. Could be an add-on.
Mei (Eng): Network peering adds ops complexity but doable as paid add-on. Adds ~2 weeks to pilot scope.
Alex (Product): Good. If you have objections, flag here now; otherwise I'll draft the proposal and circulate.
Jordan (Finance): No objections. Please include break-even timeline in doc.
Sam (Legal): Will add suggested SLA wording + credit caps.
Elena (Customer Success): I'll schedule two pilot slots and outline support handoffs.
Alex (Product): Thanks all. We'll reconvene after deliverables.
